Section 1.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 299K.07, is amended to read:

299K.07 NOTIFICATION TO[+ STATE+] EMERGENCY [-MANAGEMENT-][+ OPERATIONS+] CENTER.
(a) The notification of the commission required under the federal act must be made to the State Emergency [-Management-][+ Operations+] Center. (1) a hazardous substance on the list established under United States Code, title 42, section 9602; or
(2) an extremely hazardous substance on the list established under United States Code, title 42, section 11002.
(b) This section does not apply to a release that results in exposure to persons solely within the site or sites on which a facility is located or to a release specifically authorized by state law.

No state agency may adopt a rule or guideline that requires a person who notifies the [+State +]Emergency [-Management-][+ Operations+] Center to also notify that agency. The commissioner of each affected state agency [-shall-][+ must+] include the telephone number of the [+State +]Emergency [-Management-][+ Operations+] Center in all files, permits, correspondence, educational publications, and other communications with the public and other persons[-,-] and [-shall-][+ must+] designate personnel to coordinate receipt of reports or notifications with [+State +]Emergency [-Management-][+ Operations+] Center personnel.

[+(d) Immediately after reporting to or notifying the State Emergency Operations Center under paragraph (a) or (c), the owner or operator of a facility whose primary purpose is the processing of crude oil into petroleum products, as defined in section 296A.01, subdivision 42, must also notify the local emergency personnel with responsibility to protect public health by responding to a discharge, release, or incident from the facility. +]

bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to public safety; requiring certain facilities to notify local emergency responders of a hazardous chemical release; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 299K.07.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 299K.07, is amended to read:

299K.07 NOTIFICATION TO STATE EMERGENCY OPERATIONS CENTER.
(a) The notification of the commission required under the federal act must be made to the State Emergency Operations Center. The owner or operator of a facility must immediately notify the State Emergency Operations Center of the release of a reportable quantity of the following materials:
(1) a hazardous substance on the list established under United States Code, title 42, section 9602; or
(2) an extremely hazardous substance on the list established under United States Code, title 42, section 11002.
(b) This section does not apply to a release that results in exposure to persons solely within the site or sites on which a facility is located or to a release specifically authorized by state law.
(c) A person who is required to report to or notify a state agency of a discharge, release, or incident under section 221.0341, this chapter, chapter 18B, 18C, 18D, 115, 115A, 115B, 115C, 115D, 116, or 299J, or any other statute, administrative rule, or federal regulation may satisfy the requirement to report by notifying the State Emergency Operations Center established in this section. The commissioner of public safety must ensure that the center is staffed with adequate personnel to answer all calls 24 hours a day and that those staff are adequately trained to efficiently notify all appropriate state and federal agencies with jurisdiction over the discharge or release and provide emergency responder information. No state agency may adopt a rule or guideline that requires a person who notifies the State Emergency Operations Center to also notify that agency. The commissioner of each affected state agency must include the telephone number of the State Emergency Operations Center in all files, permits, correspondence, educational publications, and other communications with the public and other persons and must designate personnel to coordinate receipt of reports or notifications with State Emergency Operations Center personnel.

(d) Immediately after reporting to or notifying the State Emergency Operations Center under paragraph (a) or (c), the owner or operator of a facility whose primary purpose is the processing of crude oil into petroleum products, as defined in section 296A.01, subdivision 42, must also notify the local emergency personnel with responsibility to protect public health by responding to a discharge, release, or incident from the facility.

EFFECTIVE DATE.

This section is effective the day following final enactment and applies to a discharge, release, or incident occurring on or after that date.
additions: (d) Immediately after reporting to or notifying the State Emergency Operations Center under paragraph (a) or (c), the owner or operator of a facility whose primary purpose is the processing of crude oil into petroleum products, as defined in section 296A.01, subdivision 42, must also notify the local emergency personnel with responsibility to protect public health by responding to a discharge, release, or incident from the facility.
This section is effective the day following final enactment and applies to a discharge, release, or incident occurring on or after that date.
